subject: Post-call: Helix Therapeutics — inference capacity comparison & next tests
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walker <ben.walker@helixtx.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixtx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Helix Therapeutics — inference capacity comparison & next tests

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. High-level notes from our call: Helix is focused on predictable tail latency for clinical scoring (p99 targets), and prefers reserved monthly commitments for cost predictability. You also called out the need to validate both a dedicated-reserved configuration and a hyperscaler-backed reserved instance setup for procurement evaluation.

Recap (short):
- Workload: batch of short clinical documents (~128 tokens avg), bursty daytime traffic with predictable nightly backlog; peak concurrent requests ~300
- Acceptance criteria you emphasized: p50/p95/p99, startup/cold-cache behaviour, model-quality parity vs your baseline, and a cost per 1M tokens comparison
- Security asks: VPC peering + SOC2 evidence (we'll include)

Proposed next tests (attached matrix):
1) Baseline hosted run (Redwood hosted) — measure p50/p95/p99, throughput at steady-state and during 3x burst window.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) trial — configure a dedicated pool equivalent to 4x A100-class GPUs, run 24/7 for a 7-day window to measure stability and queueing behaviour.
3) Hyperscaler reserved comparison — provision reserved GPU instances from your preferred cloud (we can run identical request patterns to compare cost and observed tail latency under the same load).
4) Failure and fallback tests — simulate node reclamation and automatic fallback to smaller model variant; observe impact to latency and success rate.

Attachments: redwood-helix-test-matrix.xlsx (test cases + instrumentation), reserved-capacity-term-sheet.pdf (trial terms and what we can guarantee for a pilot).

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the sample dataset and a sandbox account to push traffic? (Priya - can you share the dataset export link?)
- Are you open to a 2-week reserved-capacity pilot (we recommend starting with 4x A100-equivalent)? If yes, procurement can use the attached term sheet as a starting point.
- We’ll follow up with a short technical plan from Karthik that lists exact metrics and logs we’ll collect.

I’ll block a follow-up on Monday to lock dates. Thanks — Ava

--

From: Ben Walker <ben.walker@helixtx.com>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix Therapeutics — inference capacity comparison & next tests

Appreciate the clear recap, Ava. This aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifying items from our side before we lock the pilot: 

1) Procurement will want a monthly commitment number (not just a term sheet). Can you provide an order-of-magnitude cost delta between: (a) Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) and (b) equivalent reserved instances on our cloud provider (we typically use GCP)? We don't need final pricing yet, just a ballpark for internal approval.

2) Data handling: the dataset will include PHI fields. We need confirmation of VPC-only access for the private trial and SOC2 + encryption at rest assurances.

3) Pilot window: procurement prefers a 2-week trial that can be extended to a 30-day reserved pilot if metrics look good. For the immediate trial, can Redwood guarantee no oversubscription on the dedicated pool during our window?

If you can get Karthik's planned instrumentation and a short MQA (mutual action plan) document, we'll circulate to procurement. Priya — I'll ping you to gather the dataset link after this thread.

Thanks,
Ben

On a separate note: would be helpful if the pilot includes a brief test that shows cost per token under a throttled burst versus a steady backlog — procurement likes seeing both numbers.

Ben Walker
Director, ML Platform
Helix Therapeutics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walker <ben.walker@helixtx.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix Therapeutics — inference capacity comparison & next tests

Thanks — adding technical specifics so procurement and your infra team can see what we'll measure and how. Short version: we can deliver the metrics you asked for and instrument everything with token-level and request-trace logs. Below is the proposed test plan and the exact signals we will collect.

Planned test cases (details):
A) Steady-state throughput: feed a constant 250 rps profile for 4 hours, measure p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and per-token cost.
B) Bursty window: simulate 3x traffic for 15 min every 2 hours for a 24-hour cycle; capture queue depth and request rejection rates.
C) Cold-start & KV cache warmup: redeploy model instance, then send 100 single-turn requests and measure increase in latency during first 5 minutes.
D) Reserved vs Hyperscaler parity: run identical request stream on (1) Redwood Dedicated reserved pool and (2) customer-provisioned reserved instances (we can orchestrate remote workers to hit both endpoints).
E) Fallback resilience: force eviction of one node in the dedicated pool and observe automatic routing to capacity tier B (smaller variant) — measure end-to-end success and latency changes.

Signals we'll provide: p50/p95/p99 (request), avg/gpu_util, queue_depth, token_count, model_version, request_id traces (linkable to logs), and sample outputs for quality checks. We'll also export a simple CSV summary for procurement that compares cost per 1M tokens and cost per 1,000 requests between both setups.

On procurement asks: we can provide a short pilot SLA for a 2-week window that guarantees no oversubscription of reserved capacity during the trial window (we put a hard cap for the reserved pool for that trial). The trial term sheet attached by Ava includes this language — we can make it explicit if needed.

Security: SOC2 report and VPC configuration doc are ready — I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a one-page VPC playbook in the follow-up. For PHI: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and isolated networking for the private trial.

I will also include an example command-line snippet (for your infra team) to run the identical load generation so results are reproducible:

# Example (pseudo):
# ./rlg --target https://pilot.helix.redwood.com --concurrency 250 --duration 14400 --payload sample_batch.json --trace --out csv

Let us know any additional metrics procurement needs — we can include billing-breakdown and token-usage per route.

-karthik

Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (to follow)
Attachment: vpc-playbook.pdf (to follow)

Thanks Ben — great questions. Quick commitments and timeline from our side so procurement has what it needs: 

1) Ballpark pricing: for a 2-week pilot sized at 4x A100-equivalent reserved pool, estimate ~ $18k - $26k for the pilot (depends on model quantization/profile). Hyperscaler reserved instances in GCP for equivalent capacity typically look 10-25% higher once you normalize for networking and storage — we’ll provide a formal cost sheet once you confirm the exact instance family. (This is a ballpark for procurement conversation only.)

2) Security & PHI: confirmed — we’ll run the private trial inside a VPC peering configuration with customer-managed keys. SOC2 summary and the VPC playbook will be attached to the procurement packet by EOD.

3) Oversubscription guarantee: Redwood will cap the reserved pool for your pilot window. Karthik will instrument and send the logs; we will provide a CSV cost comparison and p99 time series at the end of the pilot.

Next steps: 
- Priya: please share the dataset link and a preferred sandbox CIDR so we can prepare the VPC peering.
- Ben: if procurement can provision a tentative start date, we propose Jan 24 start for a two-week window (Jan 24–Feb 6). If that works, we'll issue the pilot order and the short MQA doc.
- I’ll send the mutual action plan + signable term sheet for your legal/procurement to review.

I'll drop a calendar invite for a kickoff call next Thursday to confirm test harness and endpoints. Thanks all — looking forward to running this.

Ava
